column2: openBIM Awards 2026: winners announced at the Tokyo Summit
column3: buildingSMART International's awards were presented on 8 October at the Tokyo Summit; the full list came out on the 12th. Qonic wins the Technology category with automatic 4D planning from openBIM data; the Italian company ACCA software was among the finalists.

column2: German federal BIM portal: release 3.14.0
column3: BIM Deutschland, Germany's national BIM centre, has published version 3.14.0 of the BIM-Portal with new features for users.

column2: BIMlogiq brings agentic AI to Revit
column3: With Argus AI, BIMlogiq introduces an assistant in Revit that acts directly on modelling tasks.

column2: Digital product passport and openBIM: new IBIMI working group
column3: IBIMI buildingSMART Italia launches a working group on the Digital Product Passport and its link with openBIM.

column2: ASSOBIM confirms its presidency
column3: ASSOBIM confirms its presidency, in continuity with the work done for the BIM supply chain.

column2: Restructura 2026: technology and AI for existing buildings
column3: The 2026 edition of Restructura opens, dedicated to the renovation of existing buildings with technology and artificial intelligence.

column2: South Tyrol: one shared BIM platform for all public bodies
column3: The IT department of the Province of Bolzano launches the tender for a BIM platform shared by 13 public bodies, including the Consortium of Municipalities, STA, WOBI and the Free University of Bolzano. Award expected in the summer, possible start of operation in 2027.

column2: Italian ministry guidelines on digital information management
column3: The Ministry publishes guidelines on BIM in public procurement: contracting authorities need an organisational act, an operational common data environment, staff trained in BIM roles and a training plan.

column2: South Tyrol: common data environment and BIM Guide presented at Eurac
column3: The Province starts the operational phase of BIM with a common data environment platform and a guide designed for public administrations. Standards are set by the provincial BIM competence centre; the platform will be opened to contracting authorities after the ongoing tender.

column2: Hong Kong aims for drawing-free construction
column3: A Construction Industry Council webinar presents the path towards sites driven directly by the model, without traditional drawings. It needs reliable models, clear information standards and suitable approval processes.

column2: Vienna: congress on digital innovation in construction
column3: On 17 September the 6th Innovationskongress of Digital Findet Stadt compares BIM, data, AI and automation across the whole building life cycle, asking which digital measures really pay off.

column2: Construction disputes: BIM and AI at the Kuala Lumpur symposium
column3: AIAC Asia ADR Week discussed dispute resolution in construction and the role of digital technologies, citing the BIM promoted by Hong Kong in public works since 2018.

column2: 30th buildingSMART Forum: digital sovereignty in construction
column3: In Berlin, experts from industry and research meet federal policymakers on the sector's digital transformation, with digital sovereignty as the central theme. A free live stream is also available.

column2: BIM BR Strategy: survey on digital maturity in social housing
column3: ABDI, the Ministry of Cities and BIM Fórum Brasil collect answers from social housing builders and developers until 19 November, to bring the national BIM strategy into housing policy (Decree 11.888/2024).

column2: Qonic puts AI agents inside its BIM platform
column3: The winner of the 2026 openBIM Award for Technology releases AI agents that work directly on the model in its cloud platform, plus an MCP server to connect your own AI assistant.

column2: BIM and sustainability: buildingSMART theme day
column3: On 10 November in Fulda, buildingSMART Deutschland discusses climate risk analysis, building resource passports, LCA and digital process chains, with two panels on buildings and infrastructure.

column2: BIMEXPO opens in Madrid as the BIM Plan enters tenders
column3: BIMEXPO and CONSTRUTEC run at IFEMA from 10 to 13 November. In the background, the state BIM Plan: from 2026, works contracts above the new EU threshold of €5.404 million require the Medium BIM level, those below (roughly from €2 million) the Initial level. Thresholds should be checked against the official text.

column2: BIM/CIM: column on IFC and conferences in three cities
column3: Japan's construction price research body publishes a four-part column on the essence of the IFC format and organises free BIM/CIM conferences in Sapporo (26 November), Morioka and Hiroshima.

column2: BIM+ Summit for Québec infrastructure
column3: On 17 and 18 November at the Centre des congrès de Québec, the summit planned by the government BIM roadmap: one day on diagnosis and convergence, one on action and commitments.

column2: Ruta BIM 2026 in Quito
column3: BIM Forum Ecuador organises Ruta BIM 2026 at the Swissôtel in Quito on 17 November: international talks and a public discussion on BIM in Ecuador, for contractors, designers, public bodies, universities and software companies.

column2: Poland is partner country at BIM World Munich
column3: At the tenth BIM World MUNICH (24–25 November, ICM), Poland is the partner country and presents projects and technologies. More than 8,000 industry professionals are expected.

column2: Shanghai: the 11th annual BIM report
column3: At the 2026 forum on BIM application in Shanghai, the city's annual report, now in its eleventh edition, was presented: BIM is moving from a design tool to digital infrastructure at urban scale.

column2: Public consultation on as-built and handover information
column3: The Construction Leadership Council and BIM in Asset Management consult until 16 October on the guide «As-Built & Handover Information: Requirements»: it applies to every project, from new builds to small replacements, and aims at reliable handover information for the whole life of the building.

column2: Building permits: from 2029 the IFC model itself will be checked
column3: Japan's Ministry of Land has set the basic plan for «BIM data review», to start in spring 2029: the IFC file will be the object of the review, checked with dedicated views and automated checks, also using AI. It adds to the review of drawings produced from BIM that started in April 2026.

column2: Qatar launches a national BIM award
column3: Closing the Qatar BIM 2026 conference, the Qatar Society of Engineers launches the Qatar BIM Award in four categories: professionals, public bodies, contractors and consultancies. Recommendations include a national BIM framework and a platform linking the public sector, private sector and universities.

column2: BIM mandate extended to public works from 50 billion won
column3: As planned in the Ministry's 2022 roadmap, in 2026 the BIM mandate covers all public works from 50 billion won upwards; the 30 billion threshold follows in 2028 and all works in 2030. The challenge now is to align deliverables and data formats across different clients.

column2: Autodesk University 2026: from assistant to AI agents
column3: Autodesk presents the new generation of Autodesk Assistant, an orchestrator of agents working across Forma, Revit and its other cloud platforms. Open questions remain on the cost of AI use and on the future of Revit compared with Forma.

column2: SAIE Bologna: IBIMI's BIMopenForum debuts
column3: At SAIE (7–10 October), IBIMI buildingSMART Italia presents BIMopenForum, an open format to show the work of its domains and working groups on standards, interoperable methods and tools, in the «Digital Construction» square.

column2: Hamburg moves towards BIM-based building permits
column3: At the buildingSMART Hamburg regional group, the case of the new Campus Rissen seen by the client and the building authority: the pilot for reviewing permits on a BIM model is part of the BIM.GOV programme.

column2: buildingSMART Tokyo Summit: the takeaways
column3: A report on the international summit at Haneda (6–8 October, more than 50 countries): open standards and data exchange are necessary, but BIM spreads only when it becomes everyday practice on sites and in technical offices.

column2: Allplan Max 2027: AI for structural engineering
column3: Allplan (Nemetschek group) brings AI to Allplan, Allplan Civil, Frilo, SCIA and SDS2: information search, model checking, reports and drawings. The company stresses that decisions and responsibility remain with the engineer.

column2: IBIMI joins the European project Skills2Decarb
column3: A three-year LIFE project (2026–2029) to close the skills gap in Italian construction towards zero-emission buildings: IBIMI brings openBIM into training standards for designers, technicians and site managers.

column2: Landscape and open spaces: the discipline BIM model enters the bSDD
column3: The «BIM-Fachmodell Landschaft und Freianlage», developed by buildingSMART and FLL for landscape architecture, can now be fully browsed in the buildingSMART Data Dictionary.

column2: Snaptrude Agent: from massing to LOD 400 model
column3: An AI agent that proposes a plan, gets the user's approval and then models: from massing alternatives up to LOD 400 models with structure, MEP and sheets.

column2: Embodied carbon: product data is needed in the model
column3: According to 2050 Materials, working with averages per material category measures the problem without solving it: carbon data for individual products should go into the BIM model while design choices are still open.

column2: Trimble Connect becomes a platform with AI agents
column3: At its Dimensions conference, Trimble brings AI into its common data environment: design options from point clouds, structural models from natural-language requests, voice site inspections linked to drawings.

column2: France: BIM in public procurement remains optional
column3: The Public Procurement Code (art. R2132-10) allows contracting authorities to require BIM but does not oblige them, and widespread adoption is slow. According to Le Moniteur, the push could come from the European revision of the procurement directives.

column2: Kazakhstan: BIM design mandatory for new buildings
column3: The government approves the 2026–2027 plan to digitalise construction: BIM mandatory for new residential and commercial buildings, digital building passports and machine-readable technical standards.

column2: Ireland: the BIM mandate reaches contractors and the supply chain
column3: From 1 January 2026 (Milestone 6 of the Irish BIM mandate), BIM requirements also apply to the contractor and its supply chain on public projects above €10 million. The threshold refers to the project entering stage 1 of the Capital Works Management Framework.

column2: openBIM tenders and competition: the Antitrust opinion
column3: With opinion AS2141 of 2 February, on a Campania Region tender for an openBIM platform, the Italian competition authority warns that requiring specific software or certifications can restrict competition. Tenders should describe the expected results based on open standards.

column2: BIM mandate in public administration: what changes in building management
column3: A Fervo study analyses the effect of the BIM mandate for public works above €2 million on the management of public assets: less fragmented documentation and more traceable management of buildings, most of them built before 1976.

column2: UNI 11337-8:2026 published
column3: The new part of the UNI 11337 series turns UNI/PdR 74:2019 into a standard: it defines a management system for digitalised processes in construction and real estate organisations, from BIM as a design method to the governance of data and information flows.

column2: 9th IBIMI Conference: record attendance
column3: In Rome, more than 500 people in the room and 100 online for «be smart, be open»: AI, digital twins and open standards at the centre of IBIMI buildingSMART Italia's national conference.

column2: Japan: review of BIM-generated drawings starts for building permits
column3: From 1 April 2026 the Ministry of Land introduced the «review of drawings produced from BIM» in building permits: the examiner also consults the IFC model and can skip consistency checks between drawings. Obayashi has already submitted several applications on the model, through a dedicated CDE.
